_comment: The SECOND ascension site (plan-ascension-sites.md C1), and the proof that a site owns its price: this stone asks for level 25 and a finished 'Thin the Orc Line', where the village stone asks for level 30. Nothing in Go compares the two numbers any more — D1 retired P1, so the only entry rule left is what a stone authors, snapshotted onto the pick when the row is clicked and re-judged when the ten-second channel lands (sys/ascension_rows.go stash → sys/skills.go applyAscension). ⚑ AUTHORED KNOB-FOR-KNOB FROM ascension-stone.json, which is where the reasoning for every body/factors value lives; only the gates, the id, the name and the lines differ. ⚑ PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED (55.2, 20.2): 7.65 units from the FrontCaptain and 5.50 from the nearest other spawn, because `E` goes to the NEAREST interactable and C3 already paid for that lesson with two conversants 3 units apart; 2.54 units clear of the nearest prop; and 6.08 from the nearest hostile spawn, so a player reading the panel is not pulled out of it by a wandering elite (combat closes a conversation, D21). ⭐ ITS GATE READS ITSELF SINCE C2: `root` carries a `lockedWhenGated` row to `catalog`, so an unqualified player is shown 'Show me the rewards. - locked: level 25 (12/25), complete "Thin the Orc Line"' instead of a vanished row. THE PRICE IS THEREFORE AUTHORED EXACTLY ONCE, in the conditions above — the fallback lines below deliberately no longer name it, because prose beside a gate goes stale the moment the gate moves (which is the duplication C1 removed from Go, one layer down). ⚑ TEXT IS PLAIN AND [PLACEHOLDER], the TownCrier convention — §8 of the archived ascension plan still owes both stones a lore write, and D4's tone stands: a life laid down, never a sacrifice extracted. ⭐ AND IT OFFERS ITS OWN THREE REWARDS (plan-ascension-sites.md C3 / D6, PO 2026-08-11), where the village stone offers eight: KeenEye, FrostShield, RimeBurst. Each is a choice rather than a subset taken at random - FrostShield is GATED (3 ascensions in this line), so a locked row differs between the two stones and not only the pickable ones; RimeBurst is DELIBERATELY SHARED with the village stone, because D4 says a key spent at one site leaves every other, and a pair of disjoint lists would leave that rule unreachable in play. ⚑ A site's list is authored, required and refused anywhere else (D5/P3), and every key in it is checked against the catalog at boot: an unknown one HARD-FAILS (P4) and an entry no site offers WARNS (P7). ⚑ [PLACEHOLDER] like every number here - the archived plan's §8 lore write is the natural moment to revisit which rewards belong at a war camp. ⭐ THE `catalog` NODE CARRIES THE SAME GATE AS THE GREETING, and it is not redundant: present() makes the FIRST node whose conditions pass the greeting, and applyGrant validates a row against its NODE, so an ungated catalog node would both show the reward list to a level-1 character and let a crafted message stash a pick below the price. The unconditional preview stays LAST (L3).
